research.job_description_summary: Infosys hires freshers (BE/B.Tech/ME/M.Tech/MCA/MSc, 2024-2026 batches, 60% or 6.0 CGPA, no active backlogs) as Systems Engineer, Specialist Programmer and Digital Specialist Engineer. Secondary sources describe an online test (aptitude, reasoning, pseudocode, and DSA coding for Specialist Programmer; Automata Fix for Digital Specialist Engineer), a technical interview (programming, DBMS, OS, project) and an HR interview. Training is at the Mysuru campus.
limitations: The official Infosys pages that could be fetched (infosys.com careers and graduates pages, last modified 2026-05-05) name programmes such as HackWithInfy, InfyTQ and Power Programmers but list no fresher roles, rounds or eligibility; the role and process description comes from a secondary aggregator (freshershunt.in, 2026-06-23), which also says the drive had closed.

The largest candidate-reported source is an anonymous aggregate on freshershunt.in (published 2026-08-19, 220 questions, 1,097 citations). Counts are user-submitted estimates; some entries are garbled, and several listed questions show no count (recorded as at least one report).
placementpreparation.io content is labelled 'sample questions' and is not attributed to candidates; it was used only as topic context.
No question reports specific to Specialist Programmer or Digital Specialist Engineer were found; those tracks use original practice questions (class D) mapped to the described focus areas.
The 2026 aptitude, pseudocode and debugging items are original practice items, not reported questions.
Package figures differ between sources and were not used.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

sources.title: Aggregated fresher interview questions with report counts
sources.reliability_note: Aggregated list with counts; the page shows no publication date (it says it updates automatically) and is marked 2026. Counts checked on 2026-10-09.

questions.prompt: The average of five numbers is 24. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 22. What is the number that was removed?
questions.relevance_to_role: Secondary sources list verbal, logical, quantitative and pseudocode sections in the Infosys online assessment.
follow_ups: What if the average had risen to 26 instead?
common_mistakes: Using 5 instead of 4 for the remaining count
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

mcq.explanation: Total = 5 x 24 = 120. Remaining total = 4 x 22 = 88. Removed number = 120 - 88 = 32.

questions.prompt: A 120 m long train crosses a signal pole in 6 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.relevance_to_role: Secondary sources list verbal, logical, quantitative and pseudocode sections in the Infosys online assessment.
questions.expected_answer: 72 km/h
follow_ups: How long would it take to cross a 180 m platform at that speed?
common_mistakes: Forgetting to convert m/s to km/h
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

questions.prompt: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Asha says, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' How is the man related to Asha?
questions.relevance_to_role: Secondary sources list verbal, logical, quantitative and pseudocode sections in the Infosys online assessment.
questions.expected_answer: Cousin
follow_ups: How would the answer change if the man were 'the son of my mother's only sister'?
common_mistakes: Calling the maternal uncle's son a brother
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

mcq.explanation: Asha's mother's brother is her maternal uncle; his son is her cousin.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous'.
questions.relevance_to_role: Secondary sources list verbal, logical, quantitative and pseudocode sections in the Infosys online assessment.
questions.expected_answer: Thorough
follow_ups: Give an antonym of 'meticulous'.
common_mistakes: Picking a word that merely sounds similar
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

mcq.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, so 'thorough' is closest.

questions.prompt: Pseudocode: x = 5; y = 0; while x > 0: y = y + x; x = x - 2; end while; print y. What is printed?
questions.relevance_to_role: Pseudocode tracing is listed for Systems Engineer assessments by a secondary source.
follow_ups: What is printed if the loop condition is x >= 0?
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.placementpreparation.io/infosys/interview-experience/.

mcq.explanation: Iterations: x=5 gives y=5; x=3 gives y=8; x=1 gives y=9; then x=-1 stops the loop. Output is 9.

questions.prompt: Check whether a given non-negative integer is an Armstrong number, meaning it equals the sum of its digits each raised to the number of digits.
questions.relevance_to_role: Armstrong-number programs appear in aggregated 2026 candidate reports for Infosys.
questions.expected_answer: Use len(str(n)) as the exponent and sum the powers.
follow_ups: How would you list all Armstrong numbers below 10^5?
questions.notes: Listed by the aggregated source without a visible count (at least one report).

coding.problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print Yes if it equals the sum of each digit raised to the power of the digit count, otherwise print No.
coding.expected_algorithm: Convert to digits and sum powers.

questions.prompt: Reverse a singly linked list and print its values from the new head.
questions.relevance_to_role: Reversing a linked list appears in aggregated 2026 Infosys candidate reports.
questions.expected_answer: Walk the list, pointing each node's next to the previous node.
follow_ups: How would you reverse only a sub-range of the list?
common_mistakes: Losing the next node before reassigning
questions.notes: Reported in the aggregated source; the I/O format is original (values are given as an array for judging).

coding.problem_statement: A singly linked list is given by its values from head to tail. Reverse it and print the values from the new head.
coding.input_format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated values.
coding.output_format: The reversed values separated by spaces.

questions.prompt: Print the first n terms of the Fibonacci series, starting with 0 and 1, and explain how you would write it recursively.
questions.relevance_to_role: A recursive Fibonacci series program is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Define F(0)=0, F(1)=1, F(k)=F(k-1)+F(k-2); memoize to avoid repeated work.
follow_ups: Why is plain recursion exponential?
questions.notes: Reported in the aggregated source; limits and format are original.

coding.problem_statement: Given n, print the first n terms of the Fibonacci series (0, 1, 1, 2, ...) separated by spaces.
coding.expected_algorithm: Recursive definition with memoization, or an iterative loop.

questions.prompt: Explain the four pillars of object-oriented programming with real-life examples.
questions.relevance_to_role: OOP concepts are the most frequently reported technical question in the aggregated Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Encapsulation: a bank account hides its balance behind methods. Inheritance: a SavingsAccount extends Account. Polymorphism: one withdraw() behaves differently per account type. Abstraction: callers use an interface without knowing the internals.
follow_ups: Where do you use abstract classes vs interfaces?
questions.notes: Reported 12 and 9 times in two variants on the source page; counted as 21 mentions.

questions.prompt: What is polymorphism? Explain compile-time and run-time polymorphism with an example.
questions.relevance_to_role: Polymorphism is reported separately from the pillars question in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Polymorphism lets one interface take many forms. Compile-time: method overloading or operator overloading. Run-time: method overriding with a base-class reference calling a subclass method via dynamic dispatch.
follow_ups: Can static methods be overridden?
questions.notes: Reported 6 times on the source page.

questions.prompt: Compare an array with a list (for example Java's ArrayList). When would you choose each?
questions.relevance_to_role: Array-versus-list is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Arrays have fixed size and contiguous memory with O(1) index access. Lists grow dynamically; insertion in the middle costs O(n) for array-backed lists. Use arrays when size is known and performance matters, lists for flexibility.
follow_ups: How does ArrayList grow internally?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
questions.relevance_to_role: Process-versus-thread is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: A process is an independent program in execution with its own address space. Threads share a process's memory and resources but have their own stack and registers, so they are lighter and communicate faster but need synchronization.
follow_ups: What problems can shared memory cause?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between TCP and UDP? Give one use case for each.
questions.relevance_to_role: TCP-versus-UDP is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable, with ordered delivery and retransmission (web, email). UDP is connectionless and has lower overhead without delivery guarantees (video calls, DNS queries).
follow_ups: Why does DNS commonly use UDP?
common_mistakes: Saying UDP is always faster for the user
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN with a small example.
questions.relevance_to_role: DBMS joins are reported in the aggregated 2026 data and listed as a sample question by another source.
questions.expected_answer: INNER JOIN returns only rows with matches in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and NULLs for unmatched right-side columns. Example: customers LEFT JOIN orders shows customers with no orders.
follow_ups: How would you find customers who never placed an order?
common_mistakes: Saying LEFT JOIN removes unmatched rows
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: Given a table Employee(id, name, salary), return the second-highest distinct salary using two different approaches.
questions.relevance_to_role: The second-highest-salary query is reported in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Approach 1: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee). Approach 2: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM Employee ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 (or DENSE_RANK() = 2). Mention NULL when no second value exists.
follow_ups: How would you generalise it to the Nth highest?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.

questions.prompt: Tell me about your project: your role, the technologies used and the biggest challenge.
questions.relevance_to_role: Project questions are among the most reported items in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Clear problem, own contribution, technologies and why, result, and one specific challenge with how it was solved.
follow_ups: What would you improve if you rebuilt it?
questions.notes: Reported 47 times on the source page.

questions.prompt: Tell me about yourself.
questions.relevance_to_role: The most frequently reported HR question in the aggregated Infosys data (100 mentions).
questions.expected_answer: A 60 to 90 second structured introduction ending with why Infosys and this role.

rubric.criterion: Own actions and reasoning are clear

follow_ups: What is one thing not on your resume?
questions.notes: Reported 100 times on the source page.

behavioral.star_guidance: Present, past, future: current studies and skills, one project or achievement, and why this role.

questions.prompt: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.relevance_to_role: Reported 41 times in the aggregated 2026 Infosys data.
questions.expected_answer: Ask two thoughtful questions, such as the training programme, how projects are allocated, or what success looks like in the first year. Do not ask only about salary.
follow_ups: Which question would you most like answered?
common_mistakes: Asking only about pay or leave
questions.notes: Reported 41 times on the source page.

questions.prompt: Why did you choose IT as a career, and why Infosys?
questions.relevance_to_role: Reported 9 times (why IT) and 6 times (why Infosys) in the aggregated 2026 data.
questions.expected_answer: Link a genuine interest in technology to specific facts about Infosys (training in Mysuru, breadth of domains, learning culture).
follow_ups: What do you know about Infosys's recent work?
questions.notes: Combined count of the two reported variants.

questions.expected_answer: Show growth tied to skills: becoming a strong engineer in five years and taking on design or leadership responsibility later, linked to what Infosys offers.
follow_ups: What skills will you build first?
questions.notes: At least one report on the source page.
